data.name: Detective Butler: Maiden Voyage Murder
data.detailed_description:
Wishlist the Sequel!


Acerca do jogo

Visual novels are story-based games, displaying characters on the screen while playing sounds and music in the background to create an immersive storytelling experience. Although most visual novels include branching paths and choices that affect the outcome of the story, Detective Butler: Maiden Voyage Murder has just one outcome. The only choice is how you choose to solve the mystery.

In 1962, a popular cruise ship goes out of business after the accidental deaths of two of its passengers. The ship remains a tourist attraction, until it sets sail again half a century later.

The CEO of a wealthy company takes his closest employees and son Gilligan on board for the maiden voyage. Gilligan happens to meet Detective Butler during the cruise, and as the two of them delve deeper into the ship's history, another incident occurs... Will Detective Butler find the culprit before it's too late? And will you be able to solve the mystery before the solution is revealed?

Meet the crew

  • Through the eyes of Gilligan, you'll get to know the members of his father's company, the workers of the cruise ship, and Detective Butler himself.

Enjoy the atmosphere

  • Hundreds of photo-filtered backgrounds and 29 lively music tracks create the backdrop for a mysterious cruise on the Pacific Ocean.

Review your notes

  • During the game, your journal will update with any relevant information regarding the suspects and any evidence found.

Solve the mystery!

  • Just like any classic fair-play detective story, the case can be solved through careful observation and deduction.

reviews.review:
Detective Butler: Maiden Voyage Murder is a short mystery visual novel that puts me on a cruise ship with a murder to solve and a strange history hanging over the whole trip. The story takes place on a ship that had been connected to two deaths back in 1962 before eventually being used as a tourist attraction. Decades later it sets sail again, and Gilligan ends up working with Detective Butler when another incident happens. I like the setup because the haunted cruise ship gives the mystery a nice atmosphere without needing a huge world or complicated gameplay.

Most of the game is about following the story, meeting the people on the ship and keeping track of the information I uncover. My journal records important details about suspects and evidence, which helps when I am trying to work out what actually happened. The investigation is not based around difficult traditional puzzles. Instead, I have to pay attention to conversations and interrogations and connect the information I am given. I think that works well for the type of mystery the game is trying to tell because I am encouraged to actually follow the case rather than just hunt for random objects.

The presentation is one of the things I enjoyed most. There are hundreds of photo filtered backgrounds, and the cruise ship gives the story a lot of different places to move between. The game also has 29 music tracks, and the soundtrack helps give the investigation a proper mystery feeling. The character artwork has a distinctive visual novel style too, and I like how the strange cast fits the slightly exaggerated tone. It does not look like a big budget detective game, but the presentation has enough personality to carry the story.

The biggest issue for me is that the original game is very linear. I do not get to make major decisions that completely change the story, and there is only one main outcome. That means I am mostly following the mystery rather than actually shaping it. I do like being able to work things out before Detective Butler gives me the answer, but I would have preferred more freedom in how I approached the investigation. There is a Choices DLC that adds branching gameplay and alternate endings, but I think the base game needs to be judged on its own rather than treating that extra content as part of it.

The short length is another thing I have mixed feelings about. It is a story that I can get through without making a huge commitment, which I actually appreciate for a free game, but it also means the characters do not always get as much development as I would have liked. I spend a lot of time learning about the suspects and their connections, but the story moves along quickly. Some of the mystery works because of that fast pace, while other parts could have benefited from giving me more time to understand the people involved.

I also think the game works better when I treat it as an interactive mystery story rather than a traditional adventure game. There is not much physical exploration or complicated gameplay, and most of my time is spent reading, listening and thinking about the evidence. That is not a problem for me because the detective story is clearly the main focus. The game also has achievements and keeps notes about the investigation, so there are a few small extras that make the experience feel more complete.

Overall, Detective Butler: Maiden Voyage Murder is a charming little mystery that I think does a good job with its setting and atmosphere. I like the haunted cruise ship, the detective story, the journal, the interrogation sections and the distinctive artwork and music. The linear structure, limited interaction and short story keep it from reaching the higher ratings I give to deeper mystery games, but I still think it is worth experiencing. For me, it works best as a relaxed detective story where I can sit down, follow the clues and see if I can figure out the case before Butler does.

Rating: 6.8/10
